en.headline: National security police arrest two over alleged incitement
en.dek: The National Security Department detained two people on Wednesday, including the founder of online outlet Boom News, over events outside Prince Edward station on 31 August.
body: Hong Kong police’s National Security Department arrested two people on Wednesday morning on suspicion of incitement by spreading disinformation, according to multiple news outlets citing police sources.

Those detained included Tang Ho-wing, known as the founder of the online outlet Boom News. Reports said officers arrested him at a residential building in Jordan and took him to Yau Ma Tei Police Station. Police linked the case to a gathering outside Prince Edward MTR station on the night of 31 August, when some people held flowers and slogans were shouted.

Police said they had earlier, on 3 September, arrested two men and one woman aged between 33 and 79 on suspicion of doing an act with seditious intention under section 24 of the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance. Combined with Wednesday’s action, outlets said at least five people have been arrested in the related investigation.
Those arrested have not been convicted. Police have not issued a detailed public statement on Wednesday’s detentions beyond what newsrooms attributed to official sources.

zh.headline: 國安處拘兩人涉發布假消息煽動 包括網媒創辦人
zh.dek: 警方國家安全處星期三早上拘捕兩人，包括網媒「爆炸頭」創辦人，指與8月31日太子站外事件有關。
body: 多家傳媒引述消息報道，警務處國家安全處星期三早上拘捕兩人，涉嫌發布假消息煽動。
被捕人士包括網媒「爆炸頭」創辦人鄧浩榮。報道指警員在佐敦一個住宅單位將他帶走，其後押往油麻地警署。警方將案件與8月31日晚上港鐵太子站外有人持花站立、現場有人叫喊口號一事聯繫。
警方較早前於9月3日，以涉嫌違反《維護國家安全條例》第24條「出於煽動意圖作出具煽動意圖的作為」，拘捕兩男一女，年齡介乎33至79歲。連同星期三的行動，傳媒指相關調查至少已有五人被捕。
被捕人士尚未被定罪。截至中午，警方未就星期三的拘捕另行發表詳細公開聲明，上述細節來自各報引述的官方消息。
